subject: Materials Science
title: Quantum Dots in Displays
description: A micro-lesson that makes Quantum Dots in Displays usable.

hook.text: A TV with a billion colors — quantum dots convert blue backlight into perfectly pure red and green.

buildup.text: CdSe quantum dots emit narrow-band light — purer colors than any phosphor, meaning a wider color gamut.

discovery.text: Core-shell structures (CdSe core, ZnS shell) boost quantum yield above 90% — almost every photon absorbed is re-emitted.

twist.text: Cadmium is toxic and regulated — the industry is shifting to cadmium-free InP quantum dots, slightly less bright.

climax.text: Quantum dot displays cover over 100% of the DCI-P3 color space — the most vivid screens commercially available.

punchline.text: Nanocrystals smaller than a virus producing the most vivid colors ever.

quiz.question: Why is the industry shifting from CdSe to InP quantum dots?
options: InP dots are brighter and cheaper
Cadmium is toxic and faces regulatory restrictions
InP dots can be made larger
